title: Latency Metric Synthesis and Normalization Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose
-------
This guide standardizes how we synthesize, normalize, and interpret latency signals across the serving stack so that dashboards, alerts, and post-incident analyses compare like-for-like. It documents the telemetry fields we require, the normalization math we use for cross-model and cross-hardware comparisons, and a step-by-step triage procedure for metric anomalies.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all runtime telemetry emitted by Redwood-serving components: dispatcher, scheduler, kernel dispatcher, KV cache, model-host pools, and the network fabric observed in the control plane.
- Target audiences: runtime SREs, profiling engineers, performance QA, and anyone authoring SLOs or dashboards.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
We observed repeated confusion when correlating percentiles across heterogeneous cohorts (different model sizes, sequence lengths, and GPU classes). Raw p95/p99 numbers are insufficient because:

- different workloads have different token distributions and tail behavior;
- kernels exhibit different steady-state vs warmup profiles;
- hardware differences (A100 vs H100 vs CPU) change latency skew and variance;
- sampling biases (e.g., production sampling favoring low-entropy requests) distort percentiles.

This document prescribes: a canonical telemetry contract, normalization transforms, recommended histogram bucketing, and an investigation checklist.

Key terms and definitions
-------------------------
- SLO unit: the atomic unit we measure against (e.g., per-token generation latency for hosted-api model X at seq_len=256).
- Cohort: grouping by {model, model_variant, region, accel_class, seq_len_bucket, customer_tier}.
- Normalized latency (L_norm): latency after applying transforms to remove known covariates used for cross-cohort comparison.

Required telemetry fields
-------------------------
All runtime spans/events used for latency synthesis must include the following attributes (table):

| field | type | description | retention/notes |
|-------|------|-------------|-----------------|
| request_id | string | unique per request | keep 30d indexed |
| customer_id | string | optional, helps cohorting | PII rules apply |
| model | string | model name + version | |
| model_variant | string | quantized/float/etc. | |
| seq_len | int | input sequence length (tokens) | use computed bucket if large |
| output_tokens | int | tokens generated | |
| accel_class | string | e.g., h100-80g, a100-40g, cpu | |
| kernel_id | string | identifier for kernel path executed | correlate to kernel telemetry |
| kernel_queue_ns | int | nanoseconds spent queued for kernel | |
| kernel_run_ns | int | nanoseconds kernel executed | |
| kv_cache_hit | boolean | true if KV cache served prefix | |
| cpu_network_ns | int | control-plane network time | |
| trace_start_ts | iso8601 | trace root start | |

(If a field cannot be present due to privacy or perf constraints, document why and propose a fallback.)

Histogram and bucket recommendations
-----------------------------------
- For raw span latency: use log-linear buckets from 0.1ms to 30s with finer granularity under 200ms.
- Emit both cumulative and delta histograms: cumulative for percentile computation, delta for rate-based anomaly detection.
- Ensure at least 100 buckets for sub-200ms region when using GPU-backed models (helps tail decomposition).

Normalization strategy (overview)
--------------------------------
We normalize in three stages: cohort alignment, per-request covariate adjustment, and variance stabilization.

1) Cohort alignment
- Define cohorts by model, accel_class, and seq_len_bucket. Only compare percentiles within cohorts by default.
- When comparing across cohorts (e.g., H100 vs A100), apply a hardware baseline multiplier derived from weekly calibration runs (see Calibration protocol below).

2) Covariate adjustment (per-request)
- Use a linear model: L_raw = beta_0 + beta_1 * seq_len + beta_2 * output_tokens + beta_3 * kv_cache_miss + epsilon.
- Fit model on a sliding 7-day window per-cohort; compute residual = L_raw - L_pred. The normalized latency L_norm = residual + cohort_median_baseline.
- For non-linear effects (e.g., seq_len^2), prefer GAMs when sample size permits; fall back to linear for small cohorts.

3) Variance stabilization
- Apply a robust transform to reduce heavy tails for visualization: use a log1p transform for dashboards but preserve raw percentiles in alerts.
- For alerting, use percentile bands on raw or residual latencies (do not alert on transformed values).

Calibration protocol (weekly lab runs)
-------------------------------------
Purpose: produce hardware multipliers and kernel mapping hints used for cross-hardware normalization.
Procedure:
1. Run synthetic trace generator against candidate hardware with canonical payload set (see /lab/bench/canonical-corpus).
2. Measure per-kernel mean and p95 across 1M tokens.
3. Compute multiplier: multiplier_h = median(p95_h) / median(p95_reference) where reference is h100-s-1.
4. Commit multiplier file to config repo: /configs/latency-calibration/<date>-<hardware>.yaml

Example calibration table
| hardware | p95 (ms) | multiplier | notes |
|--------:|---------:|----------:|-------|
| h100-80g | 12.4 | 1.00 | reference |
| a100-40g | 18.6 | 1.50 | higher variance for long seq |

Data collection checklist
-------------------------
- Ensure 100% of production API requests (for targeted services) include request_id and model.
- Turn on kernel_queue_ns and kernel_run_ns in kernel telemetry at least at sampling rate 10% for busy hosts.
- For small-volume customers, enable trace-shadowing for a 1-minute window per hour to get per-request fidelity.
- Retain high-fidelity traces for at least 14 days; aggregate histograms for 90 days.

Normalization and dashboard recipes
----------------------------------
1) Per-model dashboard (recommended):
- Panel: raw p50/p95/p99 for cohort (seq_len_bucket=128/256/512).
- Panel: normalized p95 (residual-based) plotted alongside raw p95.
- Panel: kernel queue vs run time heatmap (2D histogram).
- Annotation overlays: weekly calibration run timestamp and infra changes.

2) Cross-hardware comparison panel:
- For each hardware, plot L_norm * multiplier_h so that curves align if software effects are primary.
- Use bootstrapped confidence intervals (n=1000 resamples) for percentile estimates.

Alerting guidance
-----------------
- Avoid alerting on small cohorts (<1k requests/day) unless absolute latency is >5x SLO.
- Alert on: cohort p95 > SLO.p95 + max(3ms, 0.15 * SLO.p95) sustained for 5 minutes (or 3 minutes for high-severity routes).
- For kernel-queue spikes: alert when median(queue_ns) increases by >4x baseline and kernel_queue_ns contributes >30% of L_raw.

Investigation playbook: latency spike
------------------------------------
1) Confirm: Is the spike visible across similar cohorts? (model variant, seq_len_bucket)
2) Break down by kernel_id: query telemetry for top-5 kernel_ids by count and p95 contribution.
3) Check KV cache hit rate for the cohort during window.
4) Cross-reference infra events: GPU throttling, host OOM, noisy neighbors (see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues).
5) If kernel_queue_ns dominates, escalate to kernel scheduler on-call with: sample trace + host_id + kernel_id + timeline.
6) Document findings and update calibration or normalization model if necessary.

Example investigation CLI snippets
--------------------------------
- Pull cohort percentiles (pseudo-CLI):
  curl -s "https://telemetry.query/api/query" -d '{ "q": "select percentile(hist,95) from latency where model=\'redwood-xl\' and seq_len_bucket=256 and timestamp>now()-5m" }' | jq

- Quick map of kernel queue share (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT kernel_id, count(*) as n, p95(kernel_queue_ns) as q95_queue, p95(kernel_run_ns) as q95_run
  FROM traces WHERE model='redwood-xl' AND window='5m' GROUP BY kernel_id ORDER BY q95_queue DESC LIMIT 10;

Telemetry event example (single-line JSON for ingestion)
{
  "request_id": "r-9f2a3",
  "model": "redwood-xl-v2",
  "seq_len": 256,
  "output_tokens": 64,
  "accel_class": "h100-80g",
  "kernel_id": "k-embed-async-v3",
  "kernel_queue_ns": 1200000,
  "kernel_run_ns": 980000,
  "kv_cache_hit": false,
  "trace_start_ts": "2026-03-04T15:22:10.123Z"
}

Note: ingest as single-line JSON to minimize indexing cost; enrich later during batch pipeline.

Change control and versioning
-----------------------------
- Any change to the normalization model or cohort definitions must be recorded in the normalization registry: /configs/normalization-registry/<date>-<owner>.yaml and reviewed by profiling@redwood.com.
- Keep an audit column on dashboards noting the normalization version used.

Known limitations and caveats
----------------------------
- Residual-based normalization assumes covariates capture the majority of predictable latency. Residuals still include unobserved factors and should not be the only source for SLO enforcement.
- Calibration multipliers drift when firmware, driver, or microcode changes occur; schedule re-calibration after any infra upgrade.
- For very small cohorts, model-fitting is noisy; prefer cohort aggregation or basketed baselines.

Operational ownership and contacts
----------------------------------
- Primary owner: Runtime Profiling team (profiling@redwood.com).
- Escalation: runtime-scheduler-oncall@redwood.com (for kernel queue issues), infra-sre@redwood.com (for hardware incidents).

Appendix A — Normalization quick-reference table
--------------------------------------------------
| step | input | output | responsible |
|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | raw spans + histograms | cohorted percentiles | telemetry-pipeline |
| 2 | cohorted percentiles | fitted covariate model | profiling-job |
| 3 | residuals | L_norm time-series | dashboards |

Appendix B — Implementation notes
----------------------------------
- We prefer the profiling-job code in Go for performance; the models live in a shared library: internal/profiling/models.
- Persist fitted model coefficients to /meta/normalization/<cohort>/<date>.json for reproducibility.
- Unit tests: synthetic traces must exercise edge cases (kv cache thrash, long-tail kernels, sequence-length outliers).

Appendix C — Change log
------------------------
- 2026-01-10: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft).
- 2026-02-02: Added calibration protocol (Marcus Li).
- 2026-03-05: Finalized alert thresholds and CLI snippets (Renee O'Connor).

If you have questions or want this applied to a new dashboard/cohort, ping profiling@redwood.com or open a PR against /configs/dashboard-samples.
